feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/operations expertise. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, tighter section consolidation, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with increasing scope, budget/governance responsibility, and technical depth.  
- Strong relevance for digital strategy roles: web modernization, Drupal, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and advocacy communications are all well evidenced.  
- Writing is polished and credible overall, with specific platforms and scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M page views, 50+ publishers) adding substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: e.g., engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Reduce redundancy across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and dilute focus. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less overlap with the competencies/skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” and tighten the opening for a more executive tone.
- Emphasize senior-level outcomes and context: mission-driven, advocacy, public-sector/member organizations, and digital transformation.
- Reduce list-like channel enumeration; focus instead on leadership across web, email, social, content, analytics, and platform modernization.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital transformation, web platform modernization, editorial workflows, and content systems that support complex stakeholder environments. Strong background in advocacy and public-sector communications, with a track record of translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content and coordinated digital strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and workflow/systems language repeat heavily from Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Channel-specific lists duplicate detail already covered in Work Experience and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and communications capabilities, but it overlaps heavily with the Header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills sections. Tightening and sharpening the phrasing will make it feel more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-impact phrasing and tighten broad terms: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation”; “Cross-channel communications” instead of “Multi-channel communication.”
- Emphasize more current, differentiating strengths from recent roles: Drupal/CMS modernization, editorial governance, analytics/insights, AI-enabled search, and advocacy communications.
- Consider a more focused version: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications • Drupal/CMS modernization • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Content systems architecture • Stakeholder alignment • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia production
- Keep style consistent: use either all nouns or all noun phrases; “cross-department” is better replaced with “cross-functional.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the Header.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” repeat Topline Skills/Technical + IT content almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact recent position. Tighten the phrasing, foreground scope/ownership, and add outcomes or scale wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused bullet: “Built cross-functional digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.” Add metrics if available: number of sites, users, publishers, or turnaround improvements.
- Recast the AI bullet to emphasize leadership and novelty: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content preparation, and user-facing discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with the footer project list; avoid repeating named projects here unless adding measurable results.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes the NACo role—differentiate by stressing consulting ownership and current AI/search work.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were tighter and each bullet emphasized outcomes, team/operational scope, and what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opener with a results-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and parallel bullets: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: email/social growth, production volume, reporting adoption, time saved, governance compliance, or reduced reliance on vendors for video production.
- Recast softer bullets into business impact: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing advocacy and event production capacity” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Video” and newsletter leadership overlap with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise ownership, modernization, analytics, and governance.
- The website/microsite work also appears in Recent Projects; avoid repeating project-level detail here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to sharpen scope and progression: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine bullets and emphasize ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders, strengthening cadence, consistency and audience engagement.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Tighten systems language: “Improved editorial planning, cross-team coordination and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; avoid repeating “weekly video updates” in identical phrasing.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing leadership scope and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with more specific, differentiated bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and cross-team content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered content strategy for advocacy, member engagement, and campaigns
- Cut “public-sector and advocacy messaging” unless messaging is a target role requirement; “content strategy” or “member engagement” is stronger and less generic.
- Keep wording parallel: noun-led phrases, 5–8 words each, no overlap with technical tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with Core Competencies; refine with channel scope or operational leadership angle.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and execution themes rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, with the strongest recent items first.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Drupal platform leadership
- CMS modernization and migration
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- SharePoint and Power Pages
- Airtable-based operational systems
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- If space is tight, drop WordPress unless it is important for target roles; Drupal is much more supported by recent experience.
- Consider replacing “Technical Execution” with “Web Platforms, CMS Modernization & Automation” for a more senior framing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid overemphasizing it here unless it is a target-role differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI frameworks, executive dashboards, user behavior analysis, SEO/performance insights.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity” rather than listing every platform equally.
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive dashboards and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the full tool stack elsewhere; let Technical + IT hold the exhaustive list.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than generic production terms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level to capability-level language: “Broadcast-quality studio production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Video editing and post-production”
- Consider adding scale/ownership if accurate: “In-house studio buildout and operations” or “End-to-end event production” to reflect the Director-level studio leadership.
- Replace “virtual event production” with “hybrid event delivery” only, since both are listed and hybrid already implies virtual capability.
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid repeating “production” in every bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section for more specific sub-skills, not the same phrasing.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in NACo roles, so this section should sharpen specialization, not restate experience.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeat names only.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add level/context instead of a bare list: **Drupal (10, enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want stronger impact, replace the weakest/least relevant platform with a qualifier: **Drupal (10, 10,000+ page migration)** only if consistent with formatting elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the detailed list here and shortening/removing the platform names there.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the CV unless it supports a notable project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, with clearer signal on modern tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied delivery, e.g. “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome-oriented qualifiers instead of just tools, e.g. “API integrations for CMS/workflow automation,” “GitHub Actions for deployment workflows,” “Cloudflare Workers for edge scripting/performance.”
- Consider dropping versioned labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills are also version-specific; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid repeating it here unless tied to a specific tool or implementation use case.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow/operations capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize function, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Group by purpose for faster scanning: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue tracking: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add one short qualifier tied to recent work: “used to support cross-team publishing, campaign coordination, and operational workflows.”
- Keep only the strongest/recently used tools; consider dropping older/general collaboration apps if they weren’t central.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and workflow automation are already referenced in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating them too prominently.
- Slack/Teams are very common and low-signal unless collaboration tooling is central to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should better signal enterprise-level email platform ownership and align with the strong email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Expand slightly for specificity: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just tool names: Enterprise email automation • newsletter operations • audience segmentation
- Keep the list concise and ordered by strongest/recent relevance, with Dynamics 365 first only if you’ve used it meaningfully in recent work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about newsletters/email; avoid adding generic phrases like “email campaigns” unless tied to platform capability
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo system, consider naming it first to better match the experience section

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles on workflows, video, and team leadership. Make it more execution-focused and clearly earlier-career in scope.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, and multimedia production.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, or audience/reach metrics.
- Tighten leadership phrasing to avoid overstating seniority: replace “strengthening workflows” with “helped standardize publishing and production workflows.”
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize publishing workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia while informally guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing, not expanding the program.
- “Guidance to a digital media associate” may duplicate later leadership claims; keep it light.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since this is an older role, keep it concise and emphasize foundational digital/media impact.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to lead with the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Tighten vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” into clearer ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content supporting program communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of research projects, podcast episodes, stakeholder groups supported, or audience/reach.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program support + first podcast launch, avoiding a long list of minor duties.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
